native_retrieval.title: Woman convicted in double homicide seeks reduced sentence under NY domestic violence law - Democrat and Chronicle
native_retrieval.snippet: # Woman convicted in double homicide seeks reduced sentence under NY domestic violence law. Charlene Childers, the woman convicted for her role in the 2018 double homicide in Sodus, is asking a judge to reduce her prison sentence under New York's Domestic Violence Survivors Justice Act. Childers is scheduled to appear in Wayne County Court on Friday for the first hearing in her request for resentencing, according to the Wayne County District Attorney's Office. Childers pleaded guilty to first-degree manslaughter in 2019 for her role in planning the killings of Josh Niles and his fiancée, Amber Washburn. New York's Domestic Violence Survivors Justice Act gives judges the discretion to impose reduced sentences for eligible survivors of domestic violence if they can show the abuse they experienced was a significant contributing factor to the crime, according to the New York State Office of Indigent Legal Services. Callanan said no decision on Childers' request is expected at Friday's hearing.

native_retrieval.title: Pauline Hanson’s comments about domestic violence are more than vile. They are dangerous for women | Nicole Yade - The Guardian
native_retrieval.snippet: # Pauline Hanson’s comments about domestic violence are more than vile. They are dangerous for women. A woman in Australia is killed by someone she trusted every 11 days and misinformation about family violence does real harm to victims. On Wednesday, senator Pauline Hanson claimed domestic and family violence is “a two-way street”, blamed the cost of living for perpetrators’ actions, and suggested women experiencing abuse should simply “not put up with it”. These comments are not an aberration. That same platform can also risk lending credibility to dangerous myths about domestic and family violence. One instance, committed by anyone, is too many, but when a woman in Australia is killed by someone she trusted every 11 days, there can be no doubt where the true crisis lies. Victim-survivors and women trapped in abusive relationships may hear Hanson’s comments and believe they are alone. For people from communities that have long been the target of Hanson’s rhetoric, these comments will not be experienced in isolation.

native_retrieval.title: 'My sister is not just another statistic' - Jennie's Law is signed - BBC
native_retrieval.snippet: Jennifer Poole, a woman murdered by her former partner, will not be "another statistic" her brother has said after a new law in her name was signed off in the Republic of Ireland. Jason Poole's sister was unaware her partner Gavin Murphy had a history of domestic violence when he murdered her in her Dublin home in 2021. It will result in those convicted of domestic violence against a partner being included on a public register. "It was important to us, I suppose, because we wanted to make sure that Jennifer wasn't just another statistic, she's a 24-year-old mother of two who was loved and cherished by her whole family," he said. "If we had of had a domestic violence register available to us as a family, or her, she wouldn't have been in that relationship, and she wouldn't be in Glasnevin Cemetery today because she would have known he had a previous conviction for domestic violence.

english_retrieval.snippet:
Thus, to preserve families, the Courts should be circumspect and judicious, and should allow invocation of criminal process only when there are specific allegations with supporting materials which clearly constitute criminal offences. The Court further remarked that domestic violence and harassment does not normally happen in the spur of the moment, such acrimonious relationship would develop only in course of time. Thus, in such cases, there would normally be a series of offending acts, which [...] While quashing criminal proceedings against the accused in Geddam Jhansi v. State of Telangana 2025 SCC OnLine SC 263, the Supreme Court remarked, “In the context of matrimonial disputes, emotions run high, and as such in the complaints filed alleging harassment or domestic violence, there may be a tendency to implicate other members of the family who do not come to the rescue of the complainant or remain mute spectators to any alleged incident of harassment, which in our view cannot by itself [...] “(a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or

(b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.”
